status_summary: The US special envoy for Syria said on 2026-01-20 that the Syrian Democratic Forces' role as the main ground partner against the Islamic State had largely ended after the Syrian government joined the coalition, and that the US has no interest in a long-term military presence; an agreement of 2026-01-29, described by Al Jazeera as US-brokered, provides for integrating the SDF into the Syrian army. Al Jazeera, citing a Wall Street Journal report it could not verify, said on 2026-02-18 that the US was preparing to withdraw its roughly 1,000 remaining troops from Syria, and CENTCOM described the departure from al-Tanf as orderly and conditions-based. At the NATO summit in Ankara on 2026-07-07 the President said sanctions on Turkiye would be lifted and that he would consider selling F-35 jets; reports from July 2026 describe no formal sanctions removal or F-35 certification, and none was found later.

timeline.event: The US special envoy for Syria said on X that the SDF's role as the main anti-Islamic State ground force had ended, that an integration agreement would fold fighters into the Syrian army as individuals, and that the US has no interest in a long-term military presence.

An agreement described by Al Jazeera as US-brokered was reached on integrating the SDF into the Syrian army, after an earlier integration agreement of 2026-01-18 reported by Enab Baladi and Syrian government advances in the northeast.

The Wall Street Journal reported, as relayed by Al Jazeera (unverified), that the US was preparing to withdraw its nearly 1,000 remaining troops from Syria within about two months; CENTCOM had described the departure from al-Tanf as an orderly, conditions-based transition.

At the NATO summit in Ankara the President said sanctions on Turkiye would be lifted and he would consider selling F-35s; the report describes no executive order, formal sanctions removal or notification to Congress.

A law-firm sanctions update reported that no formal action had been taken to remove the CAATSA sanctions on Turkiye's defense industry agency and that the F-35 bar in the FY2020 NDAA still requires a certification about the S-400 systems.
